terms.shortDefinition: A named container that holds one value, which can be read or changed while the program runs. In GDScript you declare one with `var name = value`.
A piece of text, written between quotes, e.g. `"Niko Kadi"`. It stores words, labels, and messages shown to the player.
A whole-number type with no decimal point, e.g. `7` or `-3`. Used for card ranks, player counts, and array indexes.
A number that can have a fractional part, e.g. `0.5` or `3.14`. Used for timing, animation progress, and smooth motion.
A value that is either `true` or `false`. Used to track states like whose turn it is or whether a card is playable.
`if`, `elif`, and `else` statements that run different code depending on whether a condition is true. They let the game branch on card rules.
`for` and `while` blocks that repeat code, once per item or until a condition fails. Used to build a deck, deal cards, and walk a hand.
Named, reusable blocks of code that take inputs (parameters) and may return a result. They keep the codebase organized and avoid repetition.
Ordered, mutable lists accessed by index, written `[a, b, c]`. They hold a player's hand, the draw pile, or a list of card nodes.
Collections of key/value pairs, written `{ "key": value }`. Used to look things up by name, like mapping a suit string to its colour.
Blueprints that bundle data (properties) and behaviour (methods) into one type. You create instances with `ClassName.new()`.
A named set of constant integers, e.g. `enum Suit { CLUBS, DIAMONDS, HEARTS, SPADES }`. They make code readable and type-safe.
When a function calls itself to break a big problem into smaller copies of the same problem. Useful for resolving chains of jump cards.
Expressions that combine several true/false checks with `and`, `or`, and `not`. Used to test all the requirements for a valid play or a win.
Calling one function inside another so small helpers combine into bigger operations. Question/answer card pairing is built this way.
Checking whether a value is `null` (nothing) before using it, so the game never crashes on a missing card or empty pile.
Unpredictable number generation used to shuffle the deck. Godot provides `randf()`, `randi()`, and `RandomNumberGenerator`.
A variable that grows by adding to it each loop, e.g. a running penalty total. It collects a result across many steps.
A variable that increments each loop to track position or how many times something happened, e.g. counting cards in a jump chain.
Godot's built-in, Python-like scripting language. It is dynamically typed, concise, and designed for game logic and nodes.
The base building block of a Godot scene; every game object is a Node. Nodes form a tree and can have children, a parent, and a name.
The base class for all 2D UI nodes such as buttons, labels, and panels. Controls lay out and receive mouse/keyboard input.
A sharable data object, often saved to a `.tres` file. Card data (suit, rank, effect) is stored as a custom Resource.
Globally-accessible singletons loaded automatically by Godot on startup. The game-state manager (turn, piles) is an Autoload.
Saved trees of nodes, stored as `.tscn` files, that you can instance and reuse. A card, a player area, or the whole table can be a scene.
A virtual method called once when a Node enters the tree and is ready. It is the standard place to set up initial state and deal cards.
Named events a node can emit; other nodes connect functions to react. Signals decouple the emitter from the listener, like a turn-changed ping.
A design where an object is always in one of several states (e.g. DEAL, PLAY, RESOLVE) and rules govern transitions between them.
A switch-like construct that runs code based on which pattern a value matches. Used to dispatch on a card's effect type.
Objects that interpolate a property over time, easing cards into position. Created with `create_tween()` and chained with `tween_property()`.
The in-memory representation of a saved scene file. You call `instantiate()` on it to spawn a copy, e.g. a new card node.
The root class of most Godot types; provides properties, methods, signals, and metadata. Everything node- or resource-like derives from it.
A pressable UI control that emits `pressed` when clicked. Used for confirm/draw/declare actions and popup choices.
A control that displays non-editable text. Used for the player's name, hand count, penalty total, and status messages.
A node that counts down and emits `timeout` at an interval. Used for AI think-delays, turn limits, and reshuffle pauses.

A fast-paced Kenyan shedding card game played by 2–5 players with a 54-card deck (52 suited cards + 2 Jokers). Players race to play all their winning Answer cards in a single move after announcing 'Niko Kadi' in the previous round.

### Core Kadi Card Groups
- **Answer Cards (`4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10`)**: Standard scoring/matching cards and the only legal opening cards.
- **Penalty Cards (`2` = +2, `3` = +3, `Joker` = +5)**: Stackable draw penalties.
- **Question Cards (`8`, `Q`)**: Must be accompanied by a matching-suit Answer card in the same turn.
- **Jump (`J`) & Kickback (`K`)**: Skip the next player (`J`) or reverse turn direction (`K`).
- **Wild Ace (`A`)**: Overrides the active suit (`declared_suit`) or cancels an active penalty stack.

In Kadi, 2, 3, and Joker (JOK) are Penalty Cards that force the next player to draw 2, 3, or 5 cards respectively unless they counter with a same-rank Penalty Card (which forwards the stack) or an Ace (which cancels the stack).

```gdscript
func penalty_value() -> int:
    match rank:
        CardTypes.Ranks.TWO: return 2
        CardTypes.Ranks.THREE: return 3
        CardTypes.Ranks.JOKER: return 5
        _: return 0
```
In Kadi, Jack (J) cards are Jump Cards. Each Jack played skips one player in the current direction of play; the player about to be skipped can counter by playing their own Jump Card.
In Kadi, King (K) cards are Kickback Cards. Playing a King reverses the direction of play (clockwise <-> counter-clockwise), and can be countered or stacked.

In Kadi, Queen (Q) and 8 are Question Cards. A player who plays a Question Card must accompany it in the same move with a matching-suit Answer Card (or chain of Questions ending in an Answer Card), otherwise they must draw from the pile.

```gdscript
func is_question() -> bool:
    return rank == CardTypes.Ranks.QUEEN or rank == CardTypes.Ranks.EIGHT
```

In Kadi, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, and Ace (A) are Answer Cards. They can open the discard pile (except Ace), accompany Question Cards, and are the only cards on which a player can legally win the game.

```gdscript
func is_answer() -> bool:
    return rank in [4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10]
```

The mandatory declaration a player must make when they realize they can win on the NEXT round of play by playing all their remaining winning cards in a single move. Drawing a card revokes the declaration.

```gdscript
func can_win_this_turn(player_idx: int) -> bool:
    return announced_kadi[player_idx] and hands[player_idx].is_empty() and penalty_stack == 0
```
The face-down stack players draw from. When it runs out, the discard pile (minus the top card) is reshuffled into it.
The face-up stack of played cards; only the top card matters for matching the next play. It recycles into the draw pile on reshuffle.
One of the four categories of a playing card: Clubs, Diamonds, Hearts, or Spades. Stored as an enum in code.
The value of a card within its suit, from Ace through King. Determines most play and penalty rules.
A GDScript 4 annotation (`@onready var label: Label = $Label`) that defers fetching a child node reference until `_ready()` runs after the node enters the SceneTree.
A GDScript 4 annotation (`@export var rank: int = 2`) that exposes a script variable in the Godot Inspector dock so designers can view and edit it visually.
A Godot Container Control that automatically arranges its child Control nodes in a horizontal row — ideal for fanning a player's hand of `CardScene` instances.
A node that renders its 2D/Control children on a separate screen-space layer (`HUD`), keeping buttons and status labels pinned cleanly above the game table.
A dropdown UI Control node that lets the user pick from a list of selectable items, each with an integer ID — used in `DeclareSuitDialog` to pick Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, or Spades.
A node that stores and plays named animations authored in the animation editor.
A 2D region that detects overlapping bodies and areas and can override physics like gravity.
An ordered, dynamic, mutable list of values accessed by index.
A 2D node that overrides the location sounds are heard from in 2D space.
A 3D node that overrides the location sounds are heard from in 3D space.
A base resource for audio data (such as `.wav` or `.ogg` sound files) played by `AudioStreamPlayer`.
A node that plays an AudioStream at a non-positional, screen-wide volume.
A 2D-positioned audio player whose volume attenuates with distance from the Camera2D.
A 3D-positioned audio player with distance attenuation, panning, and doppler.
The abstract base class for all GUI buttons in Godot (`Button`, `TextureButton`, `CheckButton`, `OptionButton`).
A 2D particle emitter simulated on the CPU, configurable entirely from properties without a shader.
A first-class reference to a method or function, callable later with its arguments.
A 2D camera that scrolls, zooms, and limits the visible region of the scene.
A 3D camera that defines the perspective, field of view, and clip planes of a viewport.
Base class for anything 2D that can be drawn to the screen, such as Node2D and Control.
A physics body specialized for player- or code-controlled movement with built-in collision sliding.
A toggle button that displays a checkmark and a text label, like a checkbox.
A node that gives a collision object its 2D shape via a Shape2D resource.
A built-in RGBA color with floating-point channels in the 0–1 range.
A control that fills its rectangle with a single flat color.
A base control that automatically positions and resizes its child controls.
An associative container mapping hashable keys to values, like a hash map.
A singleton exposing engine version, frames, time scale, and run-mode information.
A static class for reading from and writing to files on disk.
A 2D particle emitter simulated on the GPU for large, cheap bursts and continuous effects.
A container that arranges its children into a grid with a fixed number of columns.
A native image buffer storing raw pixel data in CPU memory before being uploaded to a `Texture2D`.
A `Texture2D` resource created dynamically from an `Image` at runtime.
A singleton providing global, polled access to the current input state and action strength.
The base class for all input events such as key presses, mouse clicks, and touch.
Godot's global table mapping named input actions (like `ui_accept`) to physical keys, mouse buttons, or touch events.
A utility class for parsing JSON text into native Variant data and back.
A 2D node that casts light and shadows onto 2D `CanvasItem` nodes.
A single-line text input field the user can type into.
The abstract base class for the game's main loop in Godot; `SceneTree` is the default implementation used by games.
A container that adds configurable margins around a single child.
A 2D-positioned node with position, rotation, scale, and a transform.
A 3D-positioned node with transform, rotation, scale, and a basis; base for 3D scenes.
A pre-parsed relative or absolute path to a node in the `SceneTree` (for example, `"HUD/PlaySelectedButton"`).
A Control that draws a styled background rectangle, used to group other UI.
The abstract base class for all 2D physics objects (`StaticBody2D`, `RigidBody2D`, `CharacterBody2D`).
A control that visualises progress from min to max as a filled bar.
The singleton holding all project-wide settings: rendering, physics, input map, and autoloads.
A 4-component mathematical structure used to represent smooth 3D rotations without gimbal lock.
The abstract base class for UI controls that represent a number within a `[min_value, max_value]` range (`ProgressBar`, `Slider`).
A built-in axis-aligned 2D rectangle defined by a position and a size.
An Object that frees itself automatically once no references to it remain.

Godot's singleton for checking and loading files from `res://` at runtime. Calling `ResourceLoader.exists(path)` before `load(path)` lets Kadi gracefully use downloaded card PNGs when present in `res://assets/cards/` and fall back to text labels if a file is missing.

```gdscript
if ResourceLoader.exists(path):
    return load(path) as Texture2D
```
The main loop that owns the scene, groups, and the root window.
A container that scrolls a single child control that is larger than the viewport.
A numerical input `Range` control with up/down step arrows.
A 2D node that draws a Texture2D, optionally split into frames or a region.
An immovable 2D physics body used for floors, walls, and other fixed collision.
A resource that defines how UI panels and buttons draw their background, rounded corners, and borders in a `Theme`.
A multi-line text editor with syntax highlighting, selection, and clipboard support.
A 2D image resource that can be sampled and drawn by CanvasItem, Sprite2D, Control, and others.

A Godot 4.3 `[[Control]]` node (`CardArt`) that renders a `[[Texture2D]]` (such as a downloaded card PNG from `res://assets/cards/` or `card_back.png`) inside UI containers.

> [!GODOT]
> Always set `expand_mode = Ignore Size`, `stretch_mode = Keep Aspect Centered`, and `mouse_filter = Ignore` on `CardArt` so high-res downloaded card packs fit your `84×120` card slot without blocking `ClickButton`!

```gdscript
@onready var card_art: TextureRect = $CardArt
func show_downloaded_art(tex: Texture2D) -> void:
    card_art.texture = tex
    card_art.visible = (tex != null)
```
A code-created interpolator that animates properties of objects over time.
A container that arranges its children in a vertical column, top to bottom.
Godot's dynamic container type capable of holding any GDScript value (`int`, `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Object`, etc.).
A built-in 2D vector of two floats used for positions, sizes, and directions.
A node that renders its child scene, handling its own drawing, input, and camera.
A viewport that is also an operating-system window or embedded sub-window with a title and decorations.
Holds all 2D physics space, canvas, and navigation state shared by a `Viewport`'s 2D nodes.

A single image file (e.g., `res://assets/cards/deck_sheet.png`) containing all 52 playing cards and 2 Jokers arranged in a uniform grid of rows (suits) and columns (ranks).

In Godot 4.3, you slice individual cards from a downloaded sprite sheet using an `[[AtlasTexture]]` whose `region` is set to `Rect2(col * card_width, row * card_height, card_width, card_height)`.

The dock next to the **Scene** tab in the Godot 4.3 Editor that controls how downloaded `.png`, `.svg`, `.ogg`, and `.wav` files in `res://assets/` are compressed and filtered.

> [!TIP]
> For downloaded `.ogg` sound effects (`card_slide.ogg`, `shuffle.ogg`), select the file in the **FileSystem** dock, open the **Import** tab, uncheck **Loop**, and click **Reimport** so one-shot SFX don't repeat endlessly.

A `[[Control]]` property (`mouse_filter`) that decides whether a UI node consumes mouse clicks/touch taps (`Stop`), lets them pass to parent controls (`Pass`), or ignores them completely (`Ignore`).

In `card_scene.tscn`, decorative child nodes like `CardArt` (`[[TextureRect]]`), `TopRankLabel`, and `CenterSuitLabel` must use `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` so they never steal taps from `ClickButton`!

Controls how Godot 4.3 interpolates pixels when scaling a downloaded `[[Texture2D]]` up or down.

- **Linear (`TEXTURE_FILTER_LINEAR`)**: Smooth bilinear filtering — ideal for high-resolution vector or HD playing card PNGs.
- **Nearest (`TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`)**: Crisp nearest-neighbor scaling with zero blur — mandatory for retro pixel-art card packs! Set globally in **Project -> Project Settings -> Rendering -> Textures -> Canvas Textures -> Default Texture Filter**.
A theme `StyleBox` that skins a `[[Panel]]` or `[[Button]]` using a downloaded nine-patch image texture (`res://assets/ui/button_frame.png`) instead of a flat color (`StyleBoxFlat`).
Godot 4.3's audio stream resource for `.ogg` files placed in `res://assets/audio/` (such as `card_slide.ogg`, `penalty_slam.ogg`, and `niko_kadi.ogg`), played via `[[AudioStreamPlayer]]`.
